numpy: A library for fast calculations on arrays of numbers (vectors and matrices)
np: Uses NumPy under the short name np (import numpy as np)
np.array: Makes a NumPy array (a vector or matrix)
array: Makes a NumPy array (a vector or matrix)
arange: Makes an array of evenly spaced numbers. np.arange(0, 10, 2) is 0, 2, 4, 6, 8
ones_like: Makes an array of the same shape filled with 1
column_stack: Puts 1-D arrays side by side as columns to make a 2-D array
reshape: Changes an array's shape (numbers of rows and columns). -1 means "decide automatically"
shape: An array's shape (the number of elements in each direction). (rows, columns)
ndim: The number of an array's dimensions (1 for a vector, 2 for a matrix)
size: The total number of an array's elements
dtype: The type of an array's elements (int64, float64 and so on). dtype=float makes them decimals
std: The standard deviation. ddof=1 divides by n−1 (unbiased)
var: The variance. ddof=1 divides by n−1 (unbiased variance)
ddof: Divides by n − ddof. ddof=1 gives the unbiased variance and standard deviation
axis: The direction to calculate in. axis=0 is down (per column), axis=1 is across (per row)
argmax: The position (index) of the largest value
argsort: The order of positions (indices) when sorted smallest first
where: Uses the first value where the condition holds and the second where it does not
sign: The sign (1 if positive, −1 if negative, 0 if 0)
cov: The variance–covariance matrix. rowvar=False means "each column is one variable"
cov.rowvar: False treats each column as one variable
default_rng: Makes a random number generator. With a seed, you get the same random numbers every time
normal: Random numbers from a normal distribution. normal(mean, standard deviation, count)
uniform: Random numbers from a uniform distribution (every value about equally likely)
integers: Random integers. integers(low, high, count) (high is not included)
exponential: Random numbers from an exponential distribution
choice: Picks at random from an array
ravel: Lines up a multi-dimensional array in one row
tolist: Turns it into a Python list
linalg: NumPy's linear algebra functions (det, inv, solve, eig and so on)
np.linalg: NumPy's linear algebra functions (det, inv, solve, eig and so on)
solve: Solves the linear system A x = b (faster and more accurate than inv(A) @ b)
eig: Eigenvalues and eigenvectors (the vectors are in the columns). For symmetric matrices, use eigh
eigh: Eigenvalues and eigenvectors of a symmetric matrix. Real, returned smallest first
lstsq: Solves A x ≈ b by least squares. rcond=None avoids a warning
rcond: In lstsq, the cutoff below which small singular values count as 0. None uses the new rule
svd: Singular value decomposition A = U Σ Vᵀ
norm: The length of a vector (its norm)
sqrt: Square root (element by element for arrays)
sin: Sine. Element by element for arrays
log: Natural logarithm (element by element for arrays)
